title: The AI Superfans Companies Count On to Convert the Skeptics
summary: Companies are increasingly designating internal employee "AI champions" to model and promote AI tool adoption among more skeptical colleagues, according to the Wall Street Journal. The approach aims to close a persistent gap between company-wide AI rollouts and actual day-to-day usage by giving staff peer-level advocates and support rather than relying solely on top-down mandates.

title: We Heard From More Than 1,000 Readers on State Farm's Controversial AI Makeover
summary: More than 1,000 Wall Street Journal readers responded to coverage of State Farm's effort to modernize its 104-year-old insurance business using artificial intelligence, with many expressing skepticism about AI-driven claims handling and concerns about job losses among the insurer's roughly 19,000 agents. The reaction underscores the friction large legacy institutions face when embedding AI into customer-facing operations.

title: Anthropic's Political Risks Are Real, but OpenAI's Loom Even Larger
summary: The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column argues that while Anthropic faces real scrutiny from the U.S. government, including a Commerce Department order affecting some of its models, OpenAI's larger consumer base and closer government ties expose it to comparably greater political risk over time. The column suggests targeted political pressure on individual AI labs can shift quickly as administrations and priorities change.

title: New Illinois AI Safety Law Toughens Reporting Requirements
summary: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act (SB 315) on July 6, 2026, requiring developers of large-scale AI models to report safety incidents to state authorities within 72 hours, or 24 hours for incidents posing imminent risk of death or serious injury. The law, taking effect January 1, 2027, also mandates published risk frameworks, annual third-party audits, and whistleblower protections, and is described by advocates as the strictest state-level AI safety law in the country.

title: Accenture Confirms Cyber Incident
summary: Accenture confirmed a cybersecurity breach after a threat actor using the alias "888" claimed to be selling roughly 35 gigabytes of stolen source code and cloud credentials, including RSA and SSH keys and Azure access tokens. The company said the matter was isolated and has been remediated with no impact on its operations or service delivery, but did not confirm the scope of data accessed or whether client data was affected.

title: How Claude Became Salesforce's Newest Threat
summary: The Information reports that Anthropic's Claude is increasingly displacing Salesforce's software within enterprise customers, with some smaller firms building custom applications using Claude Code and AI coding tools like Replit instead of paying for Salesforce licenses. The trend has reportedly unsettled some Salesforce employees even as the company has publicly promoted Anthropic's workplace AI tools.

title: OpenAI to Publicly Launch GPT-5.6 Family of Models on Thursday
summary: OpenAI received clearance to publicly release its GPT-5.6 model family, comprising Sol, Terra and Luna tiers, on Thursday, July 9, 2026, following a roughly two-week delay requested by the U.S. government for additional review by the Commerce Department's AI standards center. Sol is priced at $5 per million input tokens, Terra at $2.50, and Luna, the lowest-cost tier, at $1 per million input tokens.

title: Amazon Looks to Raise $25 Billion in US Bonds
summary: Amazon is seeking to raise approximately $25 billion through a new U.S. bond offering, according to The Information, as large technology companies increasingly turn to debt markets to help fund AI infrastructure and data center buildout.

title: SpaceX Stock Slides Nearly 7% as It Joins the Nasdaq 100
summary: SpaceX shares fell nearly 7% as the company joined the Nasdaq-100 index on July 7, 2026, one of the fastest inclusions on record just weeks after its stock market debut. The decline reflected a broader selloff in high-momentum space and tech stocks, consistent with a historical pattern of stocks softening after index-inclusion buying is already priced in.

title: Exclusive: China's MiniMax Plans to Launch 2.7-Trillion Parameter Model
summary: Chinese AI firm MiniMax is preparing to launch a new large language model with 2.7 trillion parameters, according to The Information, as Chinese AI developers continue to push the scale of their frontier models despite U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips.

title: Exclusive: xAI Plans to Launch New Model With Cursor as Soon as Wednesday
summary: Elon Musk's xAI and coding startup Cursor jointly released a new AI model, Grok 4.5, focused on coding and agentic tasks, touting lower costs than rival offerings. The launch, originally slated for earlier in the week, was pushed back slightly to improve the model's performance ahead of release.

title: AI Borrowers Tap a $3.5 Trillion Market Hiding in Plain Sight
summary: The Information reports that AI infrastructure companies are increasingly turning to a large but little-scrutinized corner of the bond market to finance data center buildouts, as traditional equity and venture funding falls short of the trillions of dollars needed for AI compute expansion. The financing shift raises questions among analysts about credit-risk concentration tied to AI infrastructure debt.

title: China Plans to Let Top AI Firms Buy Limited Amount of Nvidia H200 Chips
summary: China plans to allow its top AI companies to purchase a limited quantity of Nvidia's H200 chips, The Information reports, as Beijing works to balance domestic chip-supply concerns with AI firms' need for advanced computing hardware. The move follows a period in which Chinese authorities had restricted or paused approvals for H200 purchases pending government review.

title: Nvidia's New Hedge Against Chip Competitors: Partner With Them
summary: Nvidia is increasingly partnering with rival AI chipmakers rather than competing head-on, including a new joint hardware system with startup d-Matrix, and a new server rack architecture designed to run chips from Nvidia or its competitors. The Information frames this as a hedging strategy to maintain Nvidia's central role in AI infrastructure even as more chip rivals emerge.

title: The Prolonged Write-Downs in Enterprise Software Startups
summary: The Information reports that Wall Street's sell-off of enterprise software stocks resumed last week, with shares of companies including ServiceNow and Snowflake falling around 8% amid growing investor concern that AI tools are eroding demand for traditional enterprise software. The piece cites Atlanta-based real estate manager Greenleaf Management, which saved roughly $100,000 annually by replacing its Salesforce CRM with a custom application built using Replit and Claude Code.

title: Meta Lifts the Veil on Its $13-Billion Alberta Data Centre
summary: Meta announced plans to build a 2.9-million-square-foot, 1-gigawatt data center in Sturgeon County, Alberta, north of Edmonton, representing an investment of more than $13 billion and the company's first data centre in Canada. The project, expected to create more than 3,000 construction jobs and 300 permanent operational roles, is among the largest private-sector investments in Canadian history, and Meta says it will match the facility's energy use with renewable generation.

title: Air Canada Names Anko Van der Werff as New CEO
summary: Air Canada announced that Anko Van der Werff, currently president and CEO of Scandinavian Airlines (SAS), will become the airline's next president and CEO, succeeding Michael Rousseau, who is retiring after 19 years with the company effective August 31, 2026. Van der Werff previously led Avianca and brings more than 25 years of international airline leadership experience.

title: Apple's $30 Billion Chip Deal With Broadcom Explained
summary: Apple and Broadcom announced a multiyear agreement worth more than $30 billion for Broadcom to manufacture over 15 billion U.S.-made chips for Apple devices, including custom silicon, RF filters and wireless connectivity components, through at least 2031. Broadcom will invest $1.5 billion in its Colorado facility as part of the deal, described as Apple's largest domestic manufacturing commitment to date and a hedge against geopolitical and trade-policy risk in its chip supply chain.

title: Ex-AT&T Exec to Join T-Mobile US
summary: T-Mobile US announced that Chris Sambar, a more than two-decade veteran of AT&T, will join the company as Chief Enterprise Officer no later than October 14, 2026, to lead its small business, enterprise and government sales operations. The hire is part of a broader leadership reshuffle at T-Mobile that includes the departure of Chief Business and Product Officer Michael Katz.

title: Apple Loses EU Court Fight Over App Store, iOS
summary: The EU's General Court dismissed Apple's challenge to the European Commission's designation of its App Stores and iOS as "gatekeeper" platforms under the Digital Markets Act, in a ruling issued July 8, 2026. The designation requires Apple to permit alternative app stores and avoid favoring its own services, and the court separately ruled Apple's related challenge over an iMessage investigation was inadmissible.

title: SpaceX's AI Advances
summary: SpaceX's AI division (formerly xAI) is rolling out AI products aimed at businesses, building on its Grok chatbot and Colossus supercomputer infrastructure. The unit has signed major compute deals, including one with Anthropic worth roughly $1.25 billion per month through 2029, and is exploring new offerings such as no-code voice-agent tools and orbital data centers.

title: Anthropic Hits Out at China's Claim of Vulnerabilities in Claude Code
summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology said its cybersecurity platform found that several Claude Code versions released between April and June contained a security backdoor sending user location and identity data to remote servers without consent, urging users to uninstall or upgrade. Anthropic said the flagged mechanism was an experimental anti-abuse measure introduced in March to prevent unauthorized resellers and distillation, adding that access to Claude in China was never authorized in the first place.

title: Grok 4.5 Enters the AI Model Race
summary: xAI and Cursor jointly released Grok 4.5, xAI's first model launch since SpaceX's acquisition of Cursor-maker Anysphere in a $60 billion all-stock deal. The model is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, more than 60% cheaper than Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5, and is available through Cursor, Grok Build, and the SpaceXAI console.

title: Cursor Is Developing an AI Agent to Compete With Claude Cowork
summary: Cursor, the AI coding startup acquired by SpaceX/xAI in a $60 billion deal, is building a general-purpose AI agent intended to compete with Anthropic's Claude Cowork, extending its ambitions beyond coding-focused tools into broader agentic assistants for knowledge work.

title: AI Customers Consolidate SaaS Apps
summary: As enterprises increase spending on AI models from Anthropic and other providers, traditional enterprise software and IT services firms are seeing a shrinking share of technology budgets. Some corporate buyers are consolidating vendors or renegotiating SaaS contracts as AI absorbs a growing portion of overall technology spend.

title: Khosla-Backed Startup Claims Breakthrough With Largest-Ever AI Model on an iPhone
summary: A Khosla Ventures-backed startup that emerged from stealth earlier this year says it successfully ran the largest AI model yet demonstrated on an iPhone, a milestone in on-device inference that could reduce mobile applications' reliance on cloud-based AI processing.

title: America Is Blowing the AI Race. Here Are Seven Ideas To Get Back on Track.
summary: A Wall Street Journal analysis argues that America's lead in artificial intelligence, while not yet lost, is narrowing quickly as global competitors close the gap, and proposes seven policy and industry actions to help the US preserve its edge in AI development and deployment.

title: China Weighs Limits on the AI Models American Companies Love
summary: As competition for AI supremacy intensifies, Beijing is considering new restrictions on Chinese companies' use of foreign AI models, part of a broader push to strengthen the position of homegrown AI technology over American alternatives.

title: Blue Origin to Raise $10 Billion at $130 Billion Valuation
summary: Blue Origin is completing its first outside funding round, raising $10 billion at a $130 billion valuation, with roughly $2 billion coming from Jeff Bezos and about $4 billion from Coatue Management. The round follows a setback in May when a New Glenn rocket exploded during a test, with the company aiming to return the rocket to flight by the end of 2026.

title: BofA Extends $520 Million Loan to OpenAI
summary: Bank of America extended a $520 million credit line to OpenAI in recent months as the company prepares for a potential IPO, marking a shift in how the bank approaches lending to still-unprofitable AI companies. The loan makes BofA one of OpenAI's largest lenders and strengthens its position in AI-related capital markets financing.

title: US Heavyweights Laud Aduna ID Service Launch
summary: Network API venture Aduna launched an identity-verification and authentication system for the US market, backed by AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile US. The service is designed to replace SMS-based one-time passcodes, which are increasingly vulnerable to AI-driven social-engineering scams.

title: Canadian Firms Are Ready to Help With Digital Sovereignty. Their Challenge Is Getting Approved
summary: Canadian technology firms say they are positioned to help government and industry reduce reliance on foreign cloud and AI infrastructure, but face a steep challenge in securing approval for public contracts. Groups such as the Council of Canadian Innovators are pushing Ottawa to fund homegrown compute providers and prioritize domestic firms as the government develops its digital sovereignty strategy.

title: Apple Sues OpenAI, Alleging It Stole Trade Secrets
summary: Apple has sued OpenAI, alleging that former Apple employees took confidential information with them to advance OpenAI's device efforts. The suit centers on claims that departing staff carried proprietary knowledge into their new roles at the AI company. The filing adds to escalating legal and competitive tension between Apple and OpenAI in AI-powered hardware.

title: Record Companies Push to Label AI Songs on Streaming Platforms
summary: An RIAA-led coalition representing record labels and artists is pushing streaming platforms to label songs that were created using AI. The group says listener surveys show fans want transparency about whether music was AI-generated. The push is part of a broader industry effort to establish disclosure standards for AI-generated content.

title: SK Hynix Raises $26.5 Billion in Record Nasdaq Debut
summary: South Korean memory chip maker SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in its Nasdaq debut on July 10, the largest-ever U.S. listing by a foreign company, pricing American depositary receipts at $149 each. Shares jumped roughly 13-14% on their first trading day, with investor demand reportedly running at more than seven times the shares on offer. The offering reflects intense investor appetite for suppliers of the memory chips used in AI hardware.

title: OpenAI Unveils Claude Cowork Competitor, Desktop 'Superapp'
summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agent that draws on corporate data to automate tasks like building spreadsheets and presentations, along with a new desktop application. The product directly targets Anthropic's Claude Cowork and Microsoft's Copilot Cowork, and is available across desktop, web and mobile. The launch underscores intensifying competition among AI labs for enterprise customers as both OpenAI and Anthropic weigh potential public offerings.

title: Meta Courts Developers With New Muse Spark 1.1 Model
summary: Meta released Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded multimodal reasoning model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, and for the first time opened one of its in-house foundation models to outside developers through a new Meta Model API. The model shows notable gains in tool use, computer use and coding, and is priced at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens. The move signals a shift in Meta's AI strategy toward selling model access rather than only releasing models openly.

title: Anthropic's Trust Names Former Fed Chair Bernanke as New Member
summary: Anthropic appointed former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the independent body that advises company leadership and appoints board members. Bernanke, a Nobel laureate in economics, becomes the trust's fourth member, joining a health-nonprofit CEO and two national-security and international-affairs experts. Trust members hold no equity in Anthropic and are meant to help the company weigh AI's broader economic and societal effects.

title: E& offloads Vodafone stake to telecoms tycoon Niel
summary: UAE telecom group e& agreed to sell its roughly 16% stake in Vodafone Group to French billionaire Xavier Niel for close to $6 billion (about £4.4 billion), making Niel Vodafone's largest shareholder. The deal prices Vodafone shares at 112.5 pence, a 15% premium to the prior close, and gives e& a net cash return of about $1.3 billion. The transaction still requires UK security clearance and extends Niel's history of telecoms consolidation deals in Europe.

title: Netflix's binge model is backfiring
summary: Netflix is seeing steep viewer drop-off between seasons of shows released all at once, with titles like One Piece, Beef and The Night Agent losing 30-70% of their audience in later seasons. Analysts say the all-at-once release format, built to compete with linear TV, is less effective against short-form platforms like TikTok and YouTube because it lets subscribers binge a show and cancel within a month. Netflix is reportedly weighing weekly releases or a greater focus on limited series to improve retention.

title: Alberta wants to be a model for government AI and power Canada-wide adoption
summary: Alberta's provincial government has spent 18 months building in-house tools on top of Anthropic's Claude models to scan its software systems for security vulnerabilities and flag applications that need upgrading. The province has published 21 white papers on its AI projects and open-sourced the underlying code so other governments and organizations can adapt the tools. The initiative positions Alberta as a potential model for AI adoption across Canada's public sector.

title: Anthropic's Political Risks Are Real, but OpenAI's Loom Even Larger
summary: A Wall Street Journal analysis argues that while Anthropic faces genuine political risk in the U.S. -- including a Pentagon supply-chain risk listing after declining to let Claude power mass surveillance or autonomous weapons -- OpenAI's far larger consumer user base and government-linked stakes could expose it to even greater political scrutiny. The piece frames model access as an emerging factor in AI company valuations as both firms weigh potential public offerings. It adds to a wider debate over how political and regulatory risk should be priced into the AI sector.

title: Power Developer Behind OpenAI's Stargate Data Center Is In Talks to Sell Stake
summary: Lancium, the power infrastructure developer behind OpenAI and Oracle's Stargate data center campus in Texas, is in talks with major technology companies to sell a minority stake, according to The Information. The discussions reflect strong investor interest in companies that supply power capacity for AI data centers amid a broader energy crunch tied to the AI buildout. Terms of a potential deal were not disclosed.

title: Alex Karp Is Saying What Every Angry CEO Is Thinking About AI
summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp said in a CNBC interview that many corporate executives privately share his frustration with the AI industry, accusing major AI labs of charging businesses steep fees for AI tools while using client data to improve their own models, calling it a kind of "wealth tax." Karp argued that customers want to retain control over their own compute, models, data stack and competitive edge rather than ceding it to frontier AI labs.

title: How Claude became Salesforce's newest threat
summary: Small and mid-sized firms are increasingly using Anthropic's Claude to replace paid Salesforce and HubSpot seats, with one firm, Greenleaf Management, saving roughly $100,000 a year by dropping Salesforce's CRM software. What began as a cost-saving workaround is raising a broader question for the software industry about what happens to paid enterprise applications as AI models take over more of the work they were built to do.

title: Anthropic's partner problem
summary: Anthropic's push into Slack with its new Claude Tag product, which acts as a persistent AI teammate inside Slack channels, has raised concerns inside Salesforce, which owns Slack and competes with its own Agentforce and Slackbot tools. Some of Anthropic's software partners have reportedly been caught off guard as the company rolls out features that overlap with products built on its models, even as Salesforce, which paid $27.7 billion for Slack in 2021, expects to spend roughly $300 million on Anthropic tokens this year and holds about a 1% stake in the AI company.

title: AI Researchers Are Having an Identity Crisis
summary: At the International Conference on Machine Learning in Seoul, AI researchers grappled with anxiety over whether AI could eventually automate their own jobs. Princeton computer science professor Arvind Narayanan argued researchers shouldn't worry, saying AI still lacks the creativity for major research breakthroughs and that the researcher's role will shift toward generating hypotheses while AI runs the experiments, though other attendees voiced more unease, a tension that coincides with AI labs' aggressive hiring of academics from computer science, economics and philosophy departments.

title: The Hot Equity Trade Spreading Through the AI Boom
summary: Public companies are increasingly turning to at-the-market equity offerings, a flexible share-sale mechanism popular when stock prices are rising, to help fund AI infrastructure buildouts. Cloud provider IREN has authorized billions of dollars in fresh share sales, while Alphabet drew attention last month with an ATM program of up to $40 billion. The approach lets companies capitalize on rallying share prices to raise capital, betting the rally lasts long enough to cash in.

title: How Wall Street Is Financing the AI Chip Boom—and Why It Matters
summary: A fast-growing market of chip-backed debt, special-purpose vehicles, leasing deals and vendor guarantees is emerging as AI startups burn cash and struggle to secure traditional loans. Chipmakers Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom are moving beyond hardware sales to help finance their own customers, in some cases backstopping unused capacity or leasing back the chips they supplied. The Information's Deep Research team mapped the financing structures reshaping the AI buildout and their implications for hardware makers, neoclouds and AI labs.

title: Palantir's 15-Step AI Sovereignty Blueprint
summary: Palantir published a 28-page report outlining 15 steps it says companies and governments should take to protect their sovereignty and build lasting competitive advantage as AI adoption accelerates. The blueprint covers foundational data practices, model- and compute-layer decisions, and control-layer governance including permissions, auditing and cybersecurity practices. Palantir argues that many enterprises underestimate how much agency they retain over how AI is deployed inside their organizations.

title: How AI Leaders Create Competitive Advantage
summary: A BCG Institute analysis of more than 600 U.S. companies, using an outside-in measure of AI adoption rather than self-reported data, found that only 6% qualify as "AI leaders," yet those firms outperform peers by 9 percentage points in shareholder returns, driven by revenue and margin growth rather than cost-cutting. The study identified talent development as the biggest differentiator between AI leaders and laggards, with leaders' AI-fluency scores nearly tripling as adoption moves from active use to full deployment across the organization.

title: Uber's Agentic Pods Spread Across Every Function
summary: Uber's CTO said 99% of the company's engineers now use AI coding tools and more than 70% of pull requests originate from AI agents, with more than 2,500 agent skills built internally. To extend agentic AI beyond engineering, Uber created "Agentic Pods" pairing AI-proficient engineers with domain experts across the business; 16 pods ran across 16 functions in two months, in one case cutting a capital-allocation process from 15 hours to 30 minutes. Uber said the biggest surprise was how quickly engineers outside their usual domain found process improvements by rethinking workflows rather than automating isolated tasks.
